submission.hypothesis: The causal boundary blocking `local_linux -> windows_native` immutable-input execution is the hard-coupled pair in `Runtime::admit_new_task_with_inputs` (crates/ordivon-runtime-core/src/runtime/engine.rs:495-512) combined with `validate_run_request_structure`'s windows_native profile restriction (engine.rs:4914-4927). The public Tool `bind_bound` (server/mod.rs:504-538) structurally hard-fixes `execution_profile: ExecutionProfile::ContainedLocal` and never lets a caller choose `trusted_local`, so every `workspace.execBound` admission reaches `admit_new_task_with_inputs`. There, the first guard rejects any `ExecutionTarget::WindowsNative` ("windows_native immutable input bindings are not implemented in R-W2", engine.rs:501-506), and the second guard requires `execution_profile == ContainedLocal` (engine.rs:507-512). Independently, `validate_run_request_structure` rejects windows_native unless the profile is `TrustedLocal` (engine.rs:4914-4920), so even if the first guard were removed the profiles are mutually exclusive by construction — a windows_native input-bound request can never satisfy both the `contained_local` requirement and the `trusted_local` window requirement. The dispatch boundary itself (`current_execution_provider_snapshot` engine.rs:1343-1374) only raises `WindowsNativeLauncherV1` via WSL and supports `trusted_local` one-command only; `contained_local` is a Linux systemd transient-unit/sandbox profile (docs/runtime.md:147) whose cache-scoping and bind-mount semantics are not implemented for the WSL/Windows launcher. Materialization itself (`materialize_input_bindings` engine.rs:1732-1832) is profile- and target-agnostic in the Run-time-owned staging dir and is not the barrier; the barrier is the profile/target admission coupling plus the immutable-input hard-gate on `WindowsNative`.
submission.causalMechanism: workspace.execBound -> bind_bound (server/mod.rs:514-527) forces ExecutionProfile::ContainedLocal unconditionally (no caller branch to TrustedLocal). run_task_proposal_with_inputs (engine.rs:464) computes input-bound identity, then on new admission calls admit_new_task_with_inputs (engine.rs:495). That method has two coupled guards: (1) engine.rs:501 rejects ExecutionTarget::WindowsNative outright with error 'windows_native immutable input bindings are not implemented in R-W2'; (2) engine.rs:507 requires ExecutionProfile::ContainedLocal. Separately validate_run_request_structure (engine.rs:4914) only permits windows_native with ExecutionProfile::TrustedLocal. Therefore no `workspace.execBound` request can ever be admitted to windows_native: profile and target requirements are conjunctively inconsistent. Even bypassing guard (1), dispatch path current_execution_provider_snapshot (engine.rs:1356-1372) and capabilities (engine.rs:1438-1450) hard-code WindowsNative immutable_inputs=false and execution_profiles=[TrustedLocal], so windows_native contained_local has no dispatcher; the Linux systemd/contained_local sandbox (docs/runtime.md:147) has no WSL/Windows counterpart.

It must prove which guard fires first and whether the windows_native check (engine.rs:501) short-circuits the contained_local check (engine.rs:507). The follow-up structural falsifier: remove only the engine.rs:501-506 WindowsNative guard, keep the contained_local requirement and the engine.rs:4914 trusted_local-only window check, and observe whether validation still rejects the request — decoupling the two guard sites to confirm the true blocking boundary is the profile/target coupling rather than the single R-W2 guard.
